data.claim: The guard refuses a data-losing git form (git restore/git checkout --/git clean) in the primary checkout only while a tracked event shard under .ddflow/events holds uncommitted lines.
data.falsifier: REFUTED if git restore . returned None while a shard is uncommitted.
data.mechanism: forbidden.check() recognises the discard subcommand and, in the primary checkout, runs git status on .ddflow/events; any uncommitted .jsonl shard makes it return a Refusal naming commit-the-event-log-first.
data.probe_output: FAILED (git restore . returned None) before the guard; passed after
data.question: Does the PreToolUse forbidden-command guard refuse git discard forms in the primary checkout while event shards are uncommitted?

evidence.note: research R2652095067 CONFIRMED: the guard's falsifier is REFUTED if git restore . returns None while a shard is uncommitted; the probe test failed first (AssertionError: git restore . returned None) and passed after the guard was added.

Read the governing rules via brief/claim/show for fix-Ba34619983b (r-task-phase-needs-wave, r-gemini-key-load, r-everything-configurable, r-bounded-everything). The fix adds a data-aware guard to the existing forbidden-commands hook, no new knob, no dependency added.

chunk_findings.detail: The checkout guard only treats `git checkout` as a discard when a separate `--` token appears (`if sub == "checkout" and "--" in args[1:]`). Git’s pathspec checkout form does not require `--`: `git checkout .` or `git checkout .ddflow/events` discards modified tracked files in the working tree. In the primary checkout with an uncommitted appended shard such as `.ddflow/events/0001.jsonl`, running `git checkout .` causes `_git_discard()` to return `""`, so `_discard_refusal()` returns `None` and the command proceeds, silently losing the event lines and reproducing the original bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

chunk_findings.detail: The new dynamic guard omits `git stash`, even though the stated fix explicitly requires guarding stash forms. `_git_discard()` only returns non-empty for `restore`, `clean`, or `checkout` with `--`. Given a primary checkout with uncommitted event shards, `git stash push -m wip` or plain `git stash` reaches `_discard_refusal()` and is not refused by this guard; it removes the uncommitted event lines from the working tree into a stash that can later be dropped, forgotten, or otherwise lost, so the promised stash protection is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_GIT_DISCARD_SUBCOMMANDS

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `git clean -fd` must be refused solely because a tracked `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl` has uncommitted modifications. In Git, `git clean -fd` removes untracked files/directories; it does not discard unstaged changes to tracked files. Concrete input: the primary checkout has a modified tracked event shard and untracked build artifacts such as `build/`; the user runs `git clean -fd` to remove the artifacts. The guard refuses with “commit the event log first” even though clean would leave the modified event shard untouched. This encodes a false-positive overblock and does not match the stated loss mechanism for tracked event lines.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: The named regression test for Ba34619983b does not cover the discard forms called out in the bug and suggested fix, especially `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, and forced/path-spec checkout forms such as `git checkout -f`, `git checkout HEAD -- .`, or `git checkout -- .ddflow/events`. It only exercises `git restore .`, `git checkout -- .`, and `git clean -fd`. If the command matcher misses `git reset --hard` or `git stash`, the original silent event-loss bug can regress while this test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: Despite the test name saying “primary_only”, it never verifies the non-primary case. It only runs commands in the temporary repository it creates as if it were the primary checkout. Concrete missing case: a linked git worktree or another checkout containing uncommitted `.ddflow/events` changes runs `git restore .` or `git checkout -- .`; if `_discard_refusal` treats every repository as primary, the test would not catch the resulting false refusal outside the primary checkout.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: The new checkout heuristic stops at the first non-option token that does not begin with `.` or `/`, so it misses Git’s valid path-checkout form `git checkout <tree-ish> <path>` without `--`. In the primary checkout with `.ddflow/events/0001.jsonl` tracked and modified with uncommitted event lines, `_check("git checkout HEAD .ddflow/events")` makes `rest = ["HEAD", ".ddflow/events"]`; the loop sees `HEAD`, breaks, and `_git_discard` returns `""`, so `_discard_refusal` returns `None`. Git then restores `.ddflow/events/0001.jsonl` from `HEAD`, silently discarding the appended event lines—the exact bug. The same applies to `git checkout HEAD .` or `git checkout main .`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

chunk_findings.detail: The added worktree assertion does not verify the primary-only behavior for the previously confirmed finding. It creates `wt` from the just-committed branch, so `wt` has no uncommitted event-shard lines; if the `primary` check in `_discard_refusal` were removed entirely, `_check("git restore .", cwd=wt)` would still return `None`. Thus the test still cannot catch a guard that falsely refuses discard commands in non-primary checkouts whenever they have uncommitted event lines. The test should modify `.ddflow/events` inside `wt` and assert the command is allowed there.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: `-t` and `-l` are boolean `git checkout` options (`--track`, `--create-reflog`), not options whose next word is a branch name. With uncommitted event shards in the primary checkout, a legitimate branch creation such as `git checkout -l -b feature HEAD` (or `git checkout -t -b feature origin/main`) is misparsed by the new loop: the first flag consumes the following `-b`, leaving `feature` and `HEAD`/`origin/main` as two positionals, so `len(positions) > 1` makes `_git_discard` return `"checkout"` and the guard refuses. Git would only create/switch to a new branch from a start point, not discard the working tree, so this blocks a valid branch switch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_CHECKOUT_VALUED

chunk_findings.detail: The new rule that “one bare positional is judged a branch switch” lets a relative path checkout through when the command is run from a subdirectory of the primary checkout. Suppose `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl` is tracked and has uncommitted appended lines, and the command is run with cwd `primary/.ddflow/events`: `git checkout shard.jsonl` (with no branch named `shard.jsonl`). `_git_discard` sees `positions=["shard.jsonl"]`, no token starts with `.` or `/`, and `len(positions) == 1`, so it returns `""` and the guard allows the command; Git then checks the file out from HEAD and silently discards the uncommitted event lines. The same bypass occurs from `primary/.ddflow` with `git checkout events/shard.jsonl`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

data.probe: -t/-l are boolean checkout flags, not valued; _CHECKOUT_VALUED now only -b/-B/-o, so git checkout -l -b feature HEAD parses feature/HEAD as one positional (branch switch) and is not refused

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_CHECKOUT_VALUED

chunk_findings.detail: The new rule that “one bare positional is judged a branch switch” lets a relative path checkout through when the command is run from a subdirectory of the primary checkout. Suppose `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl` is tracked and has uncommitted appended lines, and the command is run with cwd `primary/.ddflow/events`: `git checkout shard.jsonl` (with no branch named `shard.jsonl`). `_git_discard` sees `positions=["shard.jsonl"]`, no token starts with `.` or `/`, and `len(positions) == 1`, so it returns `""` and the guard allows the command; Git then checks the file out from HEAD and silently discards the uncommitted event lines. The same bypass occurs from `primary/.ddflow` with `git checkout events/shard.jsonl`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

chunk_findings.detail: The checkout guard only treats `git checkout` as a discard when a separate `--` token appears (`if sub == "checkout" and "--" in args[1:]`). Git’s pathspec checkout form does not require `--`: `git checkout .` or `git checkout .ddflow/events` discards modified tracked files in the working tree. In the primary checkout with an uncommitted appended shard such as `.ddflow/events/0001.jsonl`, running `git checkout .` causes `_git_discard()` to return `""`, so `_discard_refusal()` returns `None` and the command proceeds, silently losing the event lines and reproducing the original bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

chunk_findings.detail: The new dynamic guard omits `git stash`, even though the stated fix explicitly requires guarding stash forms. `_git_discard()` only returns non-empty for `restore`, `clean`, or `checkout` with `--`. Given a primary checkout with uncommitted event shards, `git stash push -m wip` or plain `git stash` reaches `_discard_refusal()` and is not refused by this guard; it removes the uncommitted event lines from the working tree into a stash that can later be dropped, forgotten, or otherwise lost, so the promised stash protection is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_GIT_DISCARD_SUBCOMMANDS

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that `git clean -fd` must be refused solely because a tracked `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl` has uncommitted modifications. In Git, `git clean -fd` removes untracked files/directories; it does not discard unstaged changes to tracked files. Concrete input: the primary checkout has a modified tracked event shard and untracked build artifacts such as `build/`; the user runs `git clean -fd` to remove the artifacts. The guard refuses with “commit the event log first” even though clean would leave the modified event shard untouched. This encodes a false-positive overblock and does not match the stated loss mechanism for tracked event lines.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: The named regression test for Ba34619983b does not cover the discard forms called out in the bug and suggested fix, especially `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, and forced/path-spec checkout forms such as `git checkout -f`, `git checkout HEAD -- .`, or `git checkout -- .ddflow/events`. It only exercises `git restore .`, `git checkout -- .`, and `git clean -fd`. If the command matcher misses `git reset --hard` or `git stash`, the original silent event-loss bug can regress while this test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: Despite the test name saying “primary_only”, it never verifies the non-primary case. It only runs commands in the temporary repository it creates as if it were the primary checkout. Concrete missing case: a linked git worktree or another checkout containing uncommitted `.ddflow/events` changes runs `git restore .` or `git checkout -- .`; if `_discard_refusal` treats every repository as primary, the test would not catch the resulting false refusal outside the primary checkout.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_commands.py:test_discard_forms_refused_in_primary_only_while_events_uncommitted

chunk_findings.detail: The new checkout classifier treats a checkout with one non-path positional as a safe branch switch, so `git checkout -f HEAD` (and `git checkout --force HEAD`, `git checkout -f --detach HEAD`) is not classified as a discard. In a primary checkout where `.ddflow/events/0001.jsonl` has uncommitted appended lines, `_git_discard(["git", "checkout", "-f", "HEAD"])` skips `-f`, records `HEAD` as the only positional, sees no `--` and no path-looking positional, and returns `""`; the dynamic guard therefore does not refuse the command. Git's `-f`/`--force` checkout discards working-tree modifications to tracked files, so the appended event lines are lost, which is exactly the event-loss scenario the guard is meant to block.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard

chunk_findings.detail: The parser only treats `-b`, `-B`, and `-o` as valued options, so it mishandles Git's `--pathspec-from-file` checkout option. Given a primary checkout with modified `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl` and a file `paths.txt` containing the pathspec `.ddflow/events/shard.jsonl`, `git checkout --pathspec-from-file=paths.txt` (or `git checkout HEAD --pathspec-from-file=paths.txt`) restores the tracked event shard from the pathspec file and discards the uncommitted lines. The classifier skips `--pathspec-from-file=...` because it starts with `-` and is not in `_CHECKOUT_VALUED`, then sees either no positional or only `HEAD`, returns `""`, and allows the discard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden.py:_git_discard
